title: NTP Clock Drift Exceeding Threshold on Routers and Switches
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'NTP Clock Drift Exceeding Threshold on Routers and Switches' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_ntp_clock_drift_exceeding_threshold_on_routers_a` (UC-5.21.2), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — NTP Clock Drift Exceeding Threshold on Routers and Switches", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=network` sourcetype='sc4snmp:metric' where `host` satisfies `current_offset_ms` > 500 for UC-5.21.2 ('NTP Clock Drift Exceeding Threshold on Routers and Switches'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `network` / `sc4snmp:metric` events where `host` stays below `current_offset_ms` > 500, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-5.21.2.

dataSources: `index=network sourcetype=sc4snmp:metric` — SNMP polling of NTP MIB objects: `ntpSysOffset` (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.168.1.1.4, Cisco-specific) or `ntpEntStatusCurrentMode` / `ntpEntStatusStratum` from RFC 5907 NTP MIB. Also `sourcetype=cisco:ios` syslog `%NTP-4-CLOCK_SKEW_DETECTED` events. Clock offset between device and NTP peer — drift exceeding 50ms can break Kerberos, DNSSEC, and log correlation accuracy. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: SC4SNMP or SNMP Modular Input, Cisco Networks Add-on (`TA-cisco_ios`) — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=network (sourcetype="sc4snmp:metric" OR sourcetype="snmp:metric") metric_name="ntpSysOffset" earliest=-24h
| eval offset_ms=abs(metric_value * 1000)
| timechart span=1h avg(offset_ms) as avg_offset_ms max(offset_ms) as max_offset_ms by host
| untable _time host values
| rex field=host "^(?<device>.+)$"
| stats latest(avg_offset_ms) as current_offset_ms by device
| eval status=case(
    current_offset_ms > 500, "CRITICAL — " . round(current_offset_ms, 1) . "ms drift (Kerberos will fail)",
    current_offset_ms > 100, "HIGH — " . round(current_offset_ms, 1) . "ms drift (log correlation impacted)",
    current_offset_ms > 50, "WARNING — " . round(current_offset_ms, 1) . "ms drift",
    1=1, null())
| where isnotnull(status)
| sort -current_offset_ms
description: Monitors the NTP clock offset on network devices and alerts when drift exceeds operational thresholds. Even small clock drift (>50ms) degrades log correlation accuracy, and drift beyond 300ms breaks Kerberos authentication and DNSSEC validation. Network devices serving as NTP sources amplify drift to all downstream clients.
value: Monitors the NTP clock offset on network devices and alerts when drift exceeds operational thresholds. Timely UC-5.21.2 alerting on 'NTP Clock Drift Exceeding Threshold on Routers and Switches' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Poll NTP offset via SNMP (ntpSysOffset). Supplement with syslog clock skew events. Alert on drift >50ms (warning), >100ms (high), >500ms (critical).
visualization: (1) Gauge: worst fleet clock offset. (2) Table: devices with excessive drift. (3) Timechart: 30-day drift trend.

references.title: RFC 5907 — Definitions of Managed Objects for NTP

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `network`** — Planned work for 'NTP Clock Drift Exceeding Threshold on Routers and Switches' shifts `avg` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-5.21.2. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `avg` on `sc4snmp:metric`** — Scheduled automation elevates `device` without crossing `current_offset_ms` > 500. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `network` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `sc4snmp:metric`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• SNMP polling enabled on network devices with NTP MIB objects accessible.
• SC4SNMP or SNMP Modular Input polling `ntpSysOffset` every 300 seconds.
• For Cisco devices: `snmp-server enable traps ntp` to enable NTP SNMP traps.

Step 1 — Configure SNMP polling for NTP offset
Add NTP MIB objects to SC4SNMP polling profile:
```yaml
profiles:
  ntp_health:
    frequency: 300
    varBinds:
      - ['1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.168.1.1.4']  # ntpSysOffset (Cisco)
      - ['1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.168.1.1.3']  # ntpSysStratum (Cisco)
```

For standard NTP MIB (RFC 5907):
```yaml
      - ['1.3.6.1.2.1.197.1.2.1']  # ntpEntStatusCurrentMode
      - ['1.3.6.1.2.1.197.1.2.3']  # ntpEntStatusStratum
```

Step 2 — Create drift monitoring search
The primary search (above) tracks offset in milliseconds.

**Syslog-based immediate detection (complements SNMP):**
```spl
index=network (sourcetype="cisco:ios" OR sourcetype="cisco:iosxe")
  "NTP" ("skew" OR "drift" OR "offset" OR "clock.*adjust")
| rex field=_raw "offset\s*(?<offset_value>[\-\d\.]+)"
| eval offset_ms=abs(tonumber(offset_value))
| where offset_ms > 50
| stats latest(offset_ms) as current_offset by host
| sort -current_offset
```

**30-day drift trend (capacity planning):**
```spl
index=network sourcetype="sc4snmp:metric" metric_name="ntpSysOffset" earliest=-30d
| eval offset_ms=abs(metric_value * 1000)
| timechart span=1d max(offset_ms) as max_daily_offset_ms by host
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) On a router, run `show ntp status` and note the `root dispersion` and `clock offset` values. Compare with the SNMP-polled offset in Splunk.
(b) Typical healthy offset: <10ms to local stratum-1, <50ms to internet NTP peers.
(c) Introduce deliberate drift by temporarily removing all NTP peers. Verify the alert fires within one poll interval.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard ("NTP Clock Drift"):
• Row 1 — Single-value: worst clock offset across fleet (red >500ms, yellow >100ms, green <50ms).
• Row 2 — Table: devices with drift >50ms, showing current offset and status.
• Row 3 — Timechart: 30-day offset trend per device.

Alerting:
• >500ms drift on any device: Critical page — Kerberos and DNSSEC at risk.
• >100ms drift on any core/distribution device: High priority — investigate root cause.
• >50ms sustained for >1 hour: Warning — NTP peering may be degraded.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **Gradual drift increasing over days.** The hardware clock (NVRAM/battery-backed) may be failing. Check `show clock detail` for hardware vs NTP source.
• **Sudden large offset.** Upstream NTP server may have jumped. Check upstream peer health. If using internet NTP, verify no BGP hijack of NTP server IPs.
• **Offset oscillating.** Network latency to NTP peer is variable (common with internet peers). Use closer/more stable NTP sources. Consider GPS-synced stratum-1 for critical infrastructure.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how far each network device's clock has drifted from the correct time. Even a small error means security systems and log records won't match up. We alert before the drift gets big enough to cause real problems like failed logins or unreliable records.
